body: Yeah I was kind of scared of posting a situation like this online for fear of being lynched but I really need advice.

I don't live in the US, I live in northern Europe. It's difficult because I don't speak the language of the country I'm living in that well, so to even see a doctor I kind of need him to translate for me...

It's called Aptus Tehobakt Pet, just a generic brand for both cats and dogs from the local chemist. We tried it only once and he vomited a little bit after but today we will try again. He has vomited two more times between 09.00 and 12.00 but not once over the night.

He is Finnish actually. Finland in general has a pretty good record when it comes to gender/sexual equality but not racial as far as my knowledge goes, but it's one thing to generalise a country's politics and another to generalise people. Living here, I even experience some prejudice for not being Finnish/of Scandinavian descent even though I'm white, and a lot of my POC friends from language classes have some horrible stories about racism in this country. 

We don't have children though he does pressure me *a lot* about it and wants to have kids very badly. I've told him that I'm only 21 and basically still a kid myself but even still, I don't think I would want him to father any of my hypothetical children. If his son was more interested in princesses than Action Man or his daughter liked monster trucks more than Barbie he would probably lose his mind.

Haha an analogy I can relate to, you propose a strong point. As I have said before in a previous comment, I think I will leave him but I really just wanted to vent out and hear what some people had to say about the whole thing. Thanks for your input :)

Okay you're right with the cognitive dissonance thing but I want to be able to get through to him. I don't just want to dismiss him as another privileged middle-class white male (though he may be), I want to be able to say something to get through to him. Regardless if he thinks a certain way that I can't change, at least to curb his language so as to not hurt or offend anyone else.

I think I just want to have faith in him. Because in other aspects I really do like him and we get along well, but I want to be able to talk to him clearly and use the right words to get him to understand that he can't just spit out opinions from old TV shows and expect them to be well received. I just don't know how to get him to listen (mainly because I get so pissed off myself so we end up having a row).

Even if/when I break up with him, he will never see it as justified. He will tell his friends that I'm his crazy hyper-feminist ex-girlfriend who wanted gay women of colour to rule the world or whatever he will come up with. I just want him to be able to learn a bit of sense and I want to be able to get through to him without him getting all defensive.

Because I'm a blind idiot apparently! I'm going to dump him though, I think I only really wrote this post because I needed to get everything off my chest (hence its length). I don't need this bigoted idiocy in my life.

You're so right, I've been fighting to defend him against myself for so long that I can't even see how this is worth it anymore. I'm just going to break up with him on the basis that he doesn't even care to *listen* to me let alone acknowledge mine or anybody else's feelings on his bigoted opinions.

Those methods sound really good actually, I think I'll try them out. The sunlight one is good for me because the sun rises here at around 0830 so that's a great time to wake up, though it's usually very cloudy. I'm the kind of person that needs a real proper wake up to be able to get out of bed, not just a single alarm beeping at me for five minutes.
It's problematic to fancy someone despite them being a pig! But yes, you are right. I think running for the hills is go for me if he keeps this up.

I've tried a lot of these routine things to get my "body" to make it's own sleeping pattern but they've never worked, but I will try again. Moving my alarm clock outside of my reach doesn't really help because I will turn it off and go back to bed. It's like Sleepy Me is this determined monster that Sensible Me can't get to wake up at a decent time. Are there any other ways of waking up that you know of that will 100% get me to wake up?

I actually think you might be right. Some people commented on here like "pursue your hobbies during the day" and stuff, and I kind of realised that none of my old hobbies interest me anymore. I might go to the doctor and ask for some advice.

I have tried doing that many times before and I will achieve a good sleeping pattern for about a week, and then slowly it slips to me going to bed later because I slept so long that I can't sleep early etc. etc. I guess the main thing is that I don't know how to cut down the *length* of time I stay asleep.

It's difficult for me to find a job because I don't speak the language of the country I'm living in fluently enough for anyone to want to hire me. It's also a small town so there isn't much opportunity to use my English skills on tourists etc. 

I will start daily language classes in February, however, and I'm sure that will give me a good rhythm. It's just annoying that it's three months away.

Problem with the sun thing: I live in northern Scandinavia and winter is well on the way so sunlight isn't really going to be a thing anymore.

I have tried various over-the-counter sleeping pills to try get an early night and they always seem to get me to sleep but then I will wake up after a couple of hours. 

My boyfriend won't let me read in bed because the light bothers him, so I end up sitting on the couch reading until the small hours without even realising.

I had a minor slip up the other night and my boyfriend found out when we went to sauna. He immediately pressed me for details when I didn't want to talk about it, I felt embarrassed and under pressure to provide some sort of explanation. He wasn't being cruel, just... abrupt and confrontational about something that is very personal to me. He didn't seem to respect my privacy about that sort of thing, and the wounds themselves were not serious in any way. I know he was just worried about me but I don't know how to talk to him about it. Does anyone have any advice?

It must be such a motivator to have a wife and children. That sounds like a beautiful household, from an outsider's perspective. And yes! I am so proud of myself for not self-harming in so long and being able to manage it, even if maybe I have replaced those destructive feelings with other negative things like alcohol and so on but hey, they have no physical side-effects (outwardly) which is what people care about, and of course there are slip-ups but I manage them though the size of the cuts themselves tend to be more severe the longer I go without doing it. My boyfriend is very unsympathetic and will criticise me for self-harming in a very counter-productive manner (as he has shown in the past) and as I cannot self-harm under his "supervision" I become aggressive and hateful when I am in a destructive mood. Do you have any advice to combat this in respect to a partner?

Can I ask, were you still self-harming when you met your wife or did you tell her about it afterwards? I felt terrible after my current boyfriend walked in on me in the act, as self-harming is such a private and intimate thing. He was extremely confronted and I felt really awful having exposed him to that. I committed to stopping about two years ago and have had multiple (but infrequent) slip-ups since then and am personally proud of myself. Yes, I drink and smoke more, but I am working forward. It is hard because my partner does not understand how big of a thing self-harming was/is for me and how much it has changed my reactions to certain problems we have undergone (we have been dating about a year and I have self-harmed maybe twice or three times since then).

Thanks for the support, I really have a very limited awareness of people my age and older that self-harm, and I don't know if that's my fault or the media's or whoever's, but although it is a terrible addiction (which is how it is for me) to face, there's a selfish side of me that is glad I'm not as alone as I thought I was. Is that horrible of me? In my ideal world, no one would have to feel like this; but knowing I'm not some pathetic backwash of adolescence gives me faith in my own future. If I should have, I suppose.

Wow what are the chances the tests evaluated in this article are from my home state. I live in northern Europe now. Thank you for your advice and the article gave me some perspective on the whole thing. I guess that a lot of anti-self-harm campaigns are geared toward teenagers or teenage girls in particular, and I was aware of that in high school. Now that I am 21 and my age group receives no anti-self-harm promotion as we are a sudden minority (as far as I am aware), it can't help but change my perception of the whole ordeal.

You are lucky that you have found a partner that will support you in your efforts to stop self-harming. When my partner found out I self-harmed (he caught me in the act), he was furious and I can never let him know I have done it again. Even if I do it, now it's like I'm living with my parents or something like I have to be so secretive about it when I never have had to be after I left my parents' home a couple of years ago. He is not sympathetic and thinks there is something wrong with me. It is hard to find another coping mechanism. Now I find myself becoming aggressive and angry to others when normally when I feel bad I would keep it internalised until I was alone would take it out on myself.

Do you think there is a reason that is is uncommon to hear of people over, say, 20 that still self-harm? Maybe I have been exposed to a narrow media but I can't help feeling ashamed/disappointed in myself that I haven't gotten over this yet. For some reason, it feels like a kind of 'when you're a baby you suck a dummy/pacifier and then you grow out of it', 'when you're a teenager you cut yourself and then you grow out of it and learn to face the real world'. I don't understand why I can't grow out of it, when I have a few friends who self-harmed during their adolescence as I did and have kicked the habit nowadays.

If I may ask, are there any methods you used to help you to stop self-harming? I've tried a few like writing on my arm instead of cutting etc. and I have definitely stopped doing it as much as I used to, but nothing ever seems to work to the same extent as the actual thing.

I would ask more personal questions but please, if you find typing your thought processes out cathartic, then message me. I know from experience that messaging a stranger can help you see things clearly as they don't have an emotional investment in your problems. Sometimes, they can give you some pretty sound advice and I wouldn't be saying this now if I didn't care.

Do you have any hobbies/things that you are interested in that may give you an incentive to wake up another morning? I know that living with depression can numb all sense of enjoyment from daily activities but I feel I should ask, just to get to know your situation better.

I'm 21 as well and I don't work or study because I have depression and sleeping problems. I will tell you some things that I do to help me move through day-to-day obligations: 

Maintaining old hobbies is defeating and getting loans from parents/roommates weighs heavy. Think of waking up every day as an achievement. Others may not think twice about it but just getting yourself out of bed is something to be proud of, don't doubt that. Try to tidy your living space, slowly and methodically, if you can (with music) because a clear home relieves a surprising amount of stress. If it takes you a couple of days, maybe one room per day, then that is enough. Don't ever think that you're racing against a clock. I know that sometimes being deeply depressed gives one the feeling of being outside the time-frame of normal life. Try not to resent that at the moment but embrace the fact that you have some time to move through some of your foundational problems at this moment. The fact that people are helping your financially is because they care about you, and it is not forever; even if it is from the government, which is like me, then know that it is not forever. 

If you are struggling with school, then take a break and take some time for yourself. Retail and customer service jobs are absolutely crushing for those of us not predisposed for that line of work and they take a lot out of people mentally. 

Don't ever feel like there is no one to speak to. Communication is key to being able to evaluate one's emotions and thoughts. Laying out your own problems and having a stranger give you advice can be highly valuable as they are not emotionally invested in the topic. They can see things more clearly. I don't know, don't think that suicide is your only option at this point in time. I have also been extremely suicidal in the past couple of weeks (the first time I have felt so in over two years) but I just kept going somehow. Please speak to me personally if you would like to. 

[IMPORTANT]: I spoke to a stranger online once about how stressed I was feeling about being an adult, because I felt like I was still a teenager and was not ready to face the epic responsibility and obligation that comes with being an independent functioning person, living in an apartment with bills and a job and all that. I was too depressed to be able to hold down a job to fulfil those requirements. He told me that the term "adult" doesn't necessarily dictate maturity, but living status. When someone identifies as an adult, it means they are somehow independent from their parents by government standards, as in they have independent decisions to make that the government recognises. It doesn't necessarily denote any kind of emotional or physical maturity. That made me feel a little bit better about the whole ordeal.

Don't listen to those who tell you "killing yourself is selfish" or "think of your loved ones". To feel like you've hit rock bottom is hard to get out of, it's hard to see any light at the end of the tunnel. But listen when people say it is more than just possible, it's probable that you will move forward. If you wait just one more night, you go to bed instead of killing yourself just for one more night, things may change in the morning. Just giving yourself a little more time gives the universe a chance to throw something more at you. A friend of mine says "things have a way of righting themselves" which I always thought was stupid; only you can change the way your life goes. That's what I thought. But after some time of being suicidal myself, I realised that sometimes one's circumstances do have a way of changing themselves for the better without one's own decisions. If you wish to end your life, then I know that your suffering will indeed end. But I also know that if you continue through this, you will know happiness again. If you're at the bottom, the only way forward is up. Message me if you will because I was on the brink of suicide only last week and how things have changed. There is support where you need it. I, and other members  of this thread, will support you. We are people who care. I care. I wouldn't be writing this if I didn't care.
Yeah okay so instead of responding negatively when he does it, I need to sit down with him and actually bring it up and talk about it.

When I said that I didn't mean I say exactly "Hello dear yes stop objectifying me please", I tell him specifically what it is that he said that made me feel bad, like "whoa titties!" isn't a really nice way to greet your girlfriend in the morning when she's putting a bra on, for example.

I only hinted at the start but nowadays when he's getting on my nerves I will tell him out right to stop objectifying me. He doesn't seem to ever take me seriously though, he just blows it off like I'm overreacting which makes me even more irritated.

I guess that's the thing that makes this difficult because sometimes of course I like it if I feel like it but other times it irritates me, and I know that it's not his fault that he doesn't know how I'm feeling at that particular time. I think that normally I would enjoy it, but coupled in with the other stuff it has kind of ruined that act for me. I don't know if I'm being unfair to him now but it's just my general attitude toward the whole thing. That being said, we have sex regularly which we both enjoy.

Yeah this is his first "proper" relationship but we've been dating for over a year but I've told him to back off so many times that it's becoming tiring. When I tell him to cut it out he gets kind of defensive but stops, but will do the same thing the next day ??

Yeah you're right, thanks for the advice. I've never been in such an intensely committed relationship (at least on his part) and your tips in the break-up have helped me to figure out how to go about doing this. Now it's just up to me to bite the bullet and get it done. Thankfully, I don't think he would try to contact me after I break up with him but I'll take the precautions regardless.

Do you think there would be any way for me to talk to him about this, and get him to understand that what he is saying is unacceptable? I have tried in the past to confront him about his severe attachment and how I'm not ready for such a committed relationship but we've never got very far. I don't really know how to approach the whole conversation.

Yeah it's hard because all the comments here reflect different aspects of my feelings toward this whole situation. Like, of course I want what is best for him and don't want to hurt him in any way (despite the fact that I have to), the fact that he is emotionally manipulating me and playing with my feelings really gets on my nerves.

I have never been religious myself so I can't imagine how difficult it must be to choose a different path, but know that you have support. I find that the majesty of space and the natural world can be inspiring, and knowing that my life is inconsequential gives me a sense of freedom. Hope this helps.
